record.original_question: A group is said to be self-similar if it admits a faithful state-closed representation by automorphisms of a regular one-rooted m-tree for some m. Can a torsion-free finitely presented metabelian group which is self-similar contain a subgroup isomorphic to the restricted wreath product H = Z ≀ Z? It is known that Z≀Z itself is self-similar(A. C. Dantas, T. M. G. Santos, S. N. Sidki, J. Algebra, 567(2021), 564–581).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a group G self-similar if, for some integer m ≥ 2, it admits a faithful state-closed representation by automorphisms of the regular one-rooted m-ary tree (equivalently, G embeds into the automorphism group of the rooted m-ary tree in such a way that the image is closed under taking states at each vertex). Let H = Z ≀ Z denote the restricted wreath product of two infinite cyclic groups (the standard lamplighter-type wreath product Z ≀ Z, which is itself torsion-free, metabelian, and known to be self-similar).

Question: Does there exist a torsion-free finitely presented metabelian group G that is self-similar and contains a subgroup isomorphic to H = Z ≀ Z?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears to remain open. A 2025 preprint on non self-similar metabelian groups explicitly states the authors could not answer this question and conjectures that no finitely presented self-similar metabelian group contains a copy of Z ≀ Z; they prove only partial results (non-self-similarity for certain metabelian groups of Krull dimension 2). Related work shows Z ≀ Z has no faithful transitive self-similar representation but does admit a non-transitive finite-state representation of degree 3.

status_evidence.title: Non self-similar metabelian groups
status_evidence.snippet: could not find an example that answers Dantas's question ... conjecture that a finitely presented self-similar metabelian group cannot contain a copy of Z ≀ Z
status_evidence.claim: Question is explicitly stated as open and a conjectured negative answer is proposed; only partial results are obtained.

status_evidence.title: On wreath product occurring as subgroup of automata group
status_evidence.snippet: Z≀Z fails to have a faithful transitive self-similar representation of degree m, but Z≀Z has a non-transitive self-similar finite-state representation of degree 3
status_evidence.claim: Related results on self-similar representations of Z ≀ Z, supporting that the embedding question is delicate and unresolved.
